The suspect was charged with resisting arrest, obstructing official business, DUI, improper turn and driving in marked lanes. In court, the suspect's charge of resisting arrest, along with her traffic infractions of improper turn and driving in marked lanes, was dismissed. She pleaded guilty to the remaining charges of obstructing official business and DUI. She was sentenced to 270 days in jail. Two hundred and sixty days of her jail sentence were suspended, resulting in a revised sentence of five days in jail and ten days of house arrest. The court ordered her to pay $1,100 in fines and all court costs and placed her on two years of community control, as well as temporarily impounding her vehicle for 90 days.
